findings.reason: as written the node's gate cannot be satisfied for shadow_source, so a worker either blocks on an unconstructible test or fudges it, and the resolver's effect on this call site goes unmeasured.
findings.text: §16's done-when says the test "shows the resolver, shadow_source and _project_for_repository each name the mounted project for the worktree path" and that "on main, shadow_source and _project_for_repository find no project, so the test fails there", but shadow_source cannot name the mounted project on the described fixture: it returns only after matching a committed ledger record (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:218-235), and the fixture removes the very `docs/state/<project>/crew.json` that would supply one — `ledger.runs(project, root=<worktree>)` reads the worktree's own ledger and an absent ledger "reads as an empty roster at version 0" (reckon/ledger.py:_load_aggregate), so `matches` is empty and shadow_source raises the same D20 refusal with and without the fix. Both arms therefore refuse identically and the clause's "fails on main" control does not fire

findings.reason: the node's whole deliverable is "one owner"; a gate that cannot show the four call sites share it cannot distinguish a completed consolidation from a partial one, and adding a delegation assertion (patch the resolver and assert each of the four calls it) would close that gap.
findings.text: §16's done-when leads with "one function … and the four sites above call it", but the named test exercises only the new resolver plus `shadow_source` and `_project_for_repository`; it never shows that `_repository_owning_projects` or `_scope_derivation_project` route through the one owner, so a node that refactors only the two site that were broken and leaves the two already-identity-based sites duplicated still passes.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited symbol resolves: `_repository_owning_projects` (reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:518), `_scope_derivation_project` (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:153), `shadow_source` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:198), `_project_for_repository` (reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:60), `project_mount_repository` (reckon/crew/dispatch_sections.py:42), `_mounted_projects` (reckon/crew/query.py:359), `mounted_repository_projects` (reckon/crew/routing.py:3227) and `repository_identity` (reckon/crew/node.py:1340).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §16's done-when (line 120) asserts "the four sites above call it" but the named test can verify neither that clause nor, for `shadow_source`, its own negative control.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — no gate log or evidence artifact is routed to a session scratchpad or node-local temp; the node's landing record accumulates in the plan's evidence record under `docs/evidence/`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers reach the cited symbols or the section's prose; the four sites are named by their real identifiers.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the census matches the code: all four named sites are `mounted_repository_projects()` callers that resolve a repository to its projects, the two excluded sites (`project_mount_repository`, `_mounted_projects`) resolve the other direction, and the resolver's placement in `routing.py` is forced because `routing.py` imports `reckon/crew/node.py` at module scope (line 38) while `node.py` imports neither routing nor dispatch.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §16 names one deliverable: one identity-based repository-to-projects resolver with all four call sites routed through it.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s16 is declared implementable with no missing dependency; its serialization behind §14 on `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py` is declared in the open followup f-lmr-009 ("§14 and §16 both edit … so they run one at a time, §14 first"), and the plan's file-claim refusal prevents concurrent runs, so no `plan-section-depends-on` entry is required.
